Article Title: Nvidia loses $500 billion since last week amid 'spy' scandal; Jensen Huang slips to 13th on Forbes rich list
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after reports came out on multiple affairs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang, extending a weeks-long selloff in the chipmaker amid concerns over the company's leadership and the future of the artificial intelligence boom. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19.The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Its shares are now around 30 per cent below the record high touched on October 6, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market capitalisation over the past month. Nvidia's market value slipped below $4 trillion, a level it had not breached since July 2025, reported Reuters. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.The selloff marks a sharp reversal for a company that became the world's most valuable publicly listed business on the back of the global AI boom. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which power artificial intelligence systems and data centres, made it a central player in the technology industry and one of Wall Street's biggest market drivers.Its shares had surged more than 1,700% over four years before the recent correction, while its market capitalisation had briefly crossed $5 trillion.Huang's departure has also taken a toll on his personal fortune. The Nvidia co-founder, who had been among the world's 10 richest people, has seen his wealth fall sharply alongside the company's stock. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires rankings, he slipped two places from eighth to tenth earlier this week. His estimated fortune subsequently fell further, pushing him out of the top 10 to 13th position.Also read: Trump unsure woman linked to Jensen Huang was a spy; report alleges 3rd affair of ex-Nvidia CEO The fallout extended beyond Nvidia to companies closely linked to its AI ecosystem. Nvidia-backed cloud computing firm CoreWeave fell 8.1 per cent, while Nebius plunged 18 per cent after cutting its 2026 revenue forecast amid delays in adding third-party capacity. Super Micro Computer also dropped 12%. However, rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom gained more than 4 per cent each, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create opportunities for competitors.Nvidia is also due to report its quarterly results next week, with investors watching its revenue growth and outlook.The turbulence in Nvidia also played out against a volatile session on Wall Street, although the broader market managed to recover most of its early losses. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,592.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09. The Nasdaq Composite also shed 0.4% to close at 25,366.09, after falling as much as 1.6% earlier in the session. Rising oil prices following US President Donald Trump's remarks on Iran added to market pressure, with Brent crude climbing 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19. The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.

Article Title: Mumbai property owner gets Rs 50 lakh for redevelopment rights, but taxman denies her Section 54EC benefit and taxes it as ‘other income’ instead of ‘capital gains’; why ITAT gave relief
Article Text:
A Mumbai woman received Rs 50 lakh from a property developer under a redevelopment agreement. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why the court ruled in favour of property owner

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What it means for property owners

You give your property for redevelopment and get payment in lieu which you then reinvest to claim capital gains exemption. The Income Tax Department , however, classifies it as ‘income from other sources’ and adds it to your total income. What do you do?In one such case, the Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled in favour of the taxpayer, holding that the payment was consideration for granting development rights in the property and was therefore taxable under the head “Capital Gains”, rather than “Income from Other Sources”.A Mumbai woman received Rs 50 lakh from a property developer under a redevelopment agreement. She then invested the amount in Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) bonds to claim income tax exemption.However, the Income Tax Department treated the receipt as “Income from Other Sources” instead of capital gains, and denied her the benefit of the exemption claimed under Section 54EC of the Income Tax Act, 1961.She had filed her income tax return for assessment year 2011-12, declaring a total income of Rs 2,64,260. The return disclosed capital gains of Rs 99,060 and she claimed an exemption under Section 54EC for investment in REC bonds.The assessment was reopened in 2018 after the Assessing Officer formed the view that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment. Following a notice under Section 148, the woman filed another return on July 14, 2018, declaring the same income.During reassessment, the officer examined a development agreement dated August 2, 2010, entered into for redevelopment of a property.According to the agreement, the owners had agreed to allow the developer to redevelop the existing building by demolishing the structure and constructing a new one. The arrangement involved 16 family members or owners, four tenants and two additional claimants on one side, and the developer on the other.The agreement provided for aggregate monetary consideration of Rs 2 crore to the owners belonging to four groups.The woman received Rs 50 lakh as her group’s share. The owners also retained the floor space index (FSI) required to construct a total carpet area of 6,400 sq ft for their residential occupation, while the remaining development potential was to be used by the developer.The woman’s position was that the payment represented consideration for granting development rights, which constituted a capital asset. She maintained that the amount had been invested in REC bonds and that the exemption under Section 54EC was therefore available.The Assessing Officer accepted that the agreement was for development and not for sale of the property. He also held that Section 50C, which deals with stamp-duty value in certain transfers of land or buildings, did not apply because the transaction did not involve a sale of the land or building itself.However, the officer took the view that the Rs 50 lakh could not be assessed as capital gains. He reasoned that the owners retained their rights in the property and would receive premises in the redeveloped building. Since the payment was non-refundable and the underlying property remained with the owners, he treated the receipt as income from other sources.The officer accordingly added Rs 50 lakh to the woman’s income, taking it to Rs 52,64,260, and initiated penalty proceedings. The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) upheld the addition and denied the Section 54EC exemption.She then challenged the decision before the tribunal. During the pendency of the appeal, she died in early 2026. Her daughter was brought on record as her legal representative after the tribunal considered the death certificate, an affidavit and the no-objection from the other legal heir.The tribunal set aside the lower authorities’ decisions on the classification of the Rs 50 lakh receipt and directed the Assessing Officer to assess it under capital gains and allow the Section 54EC exemption in accordance with the law, subject to verification of the statutory conditions.ITAT Mumbai ruled that development rights qualify as a capital asset. Since the payment was made in exchange for transferring valuable rights linked to immovable property, it was liable to be taxed as capital gains.The tribunal further observed that once the receipt is classified under ‘capital gains’, the taxpayer’s claim for an exemption under Section 54EC cannot be rejected simply because the income tax officer had assessed it under the wrong head of income.The tribunal focused on the nature of the rights for which the developer had paid the Rs 50 lakh. It found that the payment was not an independent or gratuitous receipt but arose directly from the contractual arrangement under which development rights were granted.The order stated: “The consideration was therefore intrinsically connected with the rights parted with by the assessee and other owners in favour of the developer.”The tribunal held that development rights in immovable property are valuable rights and form part of the bundle of rights attached to ownership. Their transfer can constitute the transfer of a capital asset even when the owners do not sell the entire land or building.The tribunal explained: “However, from this finding, it does not follow that there was no transfer of any capital asset at all.”The fact that Section 50C did not apply was also not decisive. The tribunal noted that the absence of a sale of land or building did not mean that no capital asset had been transferred. The grant of development rights itself had to be considered for tax purposes.The tribunal also disagreed with the reliance placed by the lower authorities on the developer’s accounting treatment. The developer had treated the payment as revenue expenditure in its books, but the tribunal held that this could not determine how the receipt should be classified in the hands of the recipient.As the order stated: “The taxability of a receipt in the hands of the recipient has to be determined with reference to the nature of the right transferred by the recipient and not on the basis of the accounting treatment adopted by the payer.”The tribunal directed the Income Tax Department to examine whether the taxpayer had fulfilled the requirements of Section 54EC and grant the exemption if the prescribed conditions were met. Under this provision, the capital gains must be invested in eligible bonds within six months of the transfer of the property or development rights.The exemption is capped at Rs 50 lakh, and the bonds must be retained for the prescribed lock-in period, which is currently five years, compared with three years earlier.The ruling has implications for property owners involved in redevelopment. ITAT Mumbai has clarified that payments received for transferring development rights must be taxed under the head ‘capital gains’ rather than ‘income from other sources’.The tribunal has also held that taxpayers can claim an exemption under Section 54EC of the Income-Tax (I-T) Act by investing the capital gains in notified bonds, provided they meet the prescribed statutory conditions. Such an investment can lower the amount of capital gains subject to tax.The decision comes at a time when redevelopment is reshaping large parts of Mumbai and its surrounding suburbs. Thousands of residents living in ageing cooperative housing societies are signing agreements with developers, often in exchange for a mix of larger homes, cash compensation, corpus funds and other benefits.
Article Summary: A Mumbai woman received Rs 50 lakh from a property developer under a redevelopment agreement. She then invested the amount in Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) bonds to claim income tax exemption. The Income Tax Department treated the receipt as ‘Income from Other Sources’ instead of capital gains, and denied her the benefit of the exemption. Mumbai bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) has ruled in favour of the taxpayer.

Article Title: Gold price prediction today: Will gold keep falling? Check outlook for November 16, 2026 week
Article Text:
Overall, the near-term outlook remains cautious as persistent inflation, dollar strength and expectations of further monetary tightening continue.

Gold price prediction

today:

The technical bias for gold prices continues to be bearish in the near-term, says Manav Modi, Senior Analyst, Commodity Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. Here’s what he has to say:

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Gold continues to remain under pressure, after extending its decline from the November highs around Rs 145,000-146,000. The 15-minute chart indicates a sustained bearish structure, with prices consistently forming lower highs and lower lows. Gold is trading below its 20-period average near Rs 136,349, while the Bollinger Bands are positioned at Rs 137,070 on the upside and Rs 135,627 on the downside.The recent consolidation around Rs 136,000-136,500 has failed to generate a meaningful recovery, and the latest move towards the lower Bollinger Band indicates that selling pressure remains dominant. Immediate support is placed around Rs 135,500-135,600, followed by Rs 134,500 and Rs 133,000. A sustained break below Rs 135,500 could extend the decline towards these levels. On the upside, Rs 136,350 is the first hurdle, followed by Rs 137,000-137,100.A sustained recovery above Rs 137,100 could trigger short-covering towards Rs 138,000-139,000. However, the broader short-term structure is unlikely to improve meaningfully unless prices reclaim Rs 139,000-140,000.Overall, the technical bias remains bearish, with any recovery likely to encounter selling pressure near the immediate resistance zones.Gold and silver extended their decline during the week, with bullion falling nearly 4.5% and touching a more-than-one-year low, while silver declined approximately 3%, reflecting broad-based weakness across precious metals. Persistent inflation concerns, a stronger US dollar and increasingly hawkish Fed expectations continued to weigh on investor sentiment.The latest US producer price data added to these concerns, with October PPI recording its largest annual increase in four years, reinforcing the view that inflationary pressures remain persistent despite earlier expectations of moderation.Following stronger employment and consumer inflation readings, markets have increasingly priced in a 25-basis-point rate hike in December, with the possibility of further monetary tightening extending into early 2027. This has kept real yields elevated and increased the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.The US dollar index hovering around 103.5 has added another layer of pressure, making gold more expensive for overseas buyers and limiting international investment demand.Meanwhile, expectations of a prolonged restrictive monetary-policy environment have encouraged investors to reassess exposure to precious metals following their substantial earlier rally.The correction in silver has been particularly pronounced, reflecting its dual exposure to investment sentiment and industrial demand. Concerns surrounding China’s economic performance have also weighed on the metal, as uncertainty over manufacturing activity and industrial consumption raises questions about the strength of physical demand.Energy-market developments have offered some relief to the broader inflation outlook. The International Energy Agency’s assessment of improving global oil supply, despite continuing geopolitical tensions and supply disruptions, has eased concerns over persistent crude-market tightness.Moderating energy prices could gradually reduce inflationary pressure and provide the Federal Reserve with greater flexibility, although the immediate impact on gold remains limited by elevated rate expectations. Investors are also closely monitoring Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments and the upcoming FOMC minutes for further clarity on the policy trajectory.Any indication that policymakers remain concerned about persistent inflation could reinforce expectations of another rate increase, while a more balanced assessment could help stabilise bullion.Overall, the near-term outlook remains cautious as persistent inflation, dollar strength and expectations of further monetary tightening continue to outweigh gold’s safe-haven appeal.The possibility of additional rate increases into early 2027 remains a significant headwind. However, any moderation in inflation expectations, softer Treasury yields or renewed investment demand could provide opportunities for stabilisation following the sharp correction.
Article Summary: Gold continues to remain under pressure, after extending its decline from the November highs around Rs 145,000-146,000. The 15-minute chart indicates a sustained bearish structure, with prices consistently forming lower highs and lower lows. Persistent inflation concerns, a stronger US dollar and increasingly hawkish Fed expectations continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

Article Title: Energy drink or sugar? FSSAI sends notice to Red Bull over composition of beverage
Article Text:
FSSAI has given Red Bull seven days to justify its energy drink label, citing concerns over added sugar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has questioned Red Bull's classification as an "energy drink", saying its high added-sugar content could mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption. The food regulator has given the company seven days to justify the label or face a possible prohibition, news agency Reuters reported citing an official notice on Monday.The regulator raised concerns over the beverage's nutritional composition. It said a significant proportion of the product's declared energy came from added sugar, raising questions about its energy-related claims."The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation," Reuters quoted FSSAI statement as saying.The regulator also flagged the drink's consumption advisory, which says consumers should not exceed 500ml a day. It said this could give consumers the impression that drinking that quantity was safe.Red Bull contains 11 grams of sugar per 100 ml. According to the FSSAI, consuming 500 ml would mean an intake of around 55 grams of sugar, exceeding the generally recommended daily limit of 50 grams.The notice marks a fresh development in a dispute that began in June, when the FSSAI moved against the use of the "energy drink" label.Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the regulator's order in the Delhi high court, arguing that they were not given prior notice before the restrictions were imposed.Red Bull secured an interim court injunction allowing it to continue using the label. Its competitors, however, were directed to stop using it after exhausting their existing stocks.The FSSAI has challenged the relief granted to Red Bull, arguing that it gives the company "an undue commercial advantage" over rivals. The matter is scheduled to be heard in January.
Article Summary: FSSAI has given Red Bull seven days to justify its energy drink label, citing concerns over added sugar. Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the regulator's order in the Delhi high court. The matter is scheduled to be heard in January.

Article Title: China stocks hover near July 2025 lows as AI jitters hit tech shares and weaken sentiment
Article Text:
AI trade faces biggest test yet as stocks tumble across Asia

Weak factory output, spending add to concerns

AI worries spread across Asian markets

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the recent drop in technology stocks is a temporary setback? Yes No Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

China's stock markets ended lower on Monday, with technology shares leading the decline amid growing doubts over the strength of the artificial intelligence (AI) rally. Weak domestic economic data added to investor concerns, leaving key indices hovering near their lowest levels since July 2025. The CSI300 and Shanghai Composite indices fell 0.9% each.The CSI300 has lost 14% so far this year.Technology stocks led the decline, with the 5G Communication Index dropping 7.5% to its lowest level in a year. The STAR50 Index, which tracks technology-focused stocks, fell 5.2%. Zhongji Innolight, a major maker of high-speed optical transceivers used in AI data centres, lost 12.3%.The fall came as worries over the future of the global AI boom continued to weigh on markets. Nvidia's shock CEO exit last week added to the uncertainty, with investors now waiting for the company's earnings report and Anthropic's IPO later this week to assess the strength of the AI-driven rally.China's economic data also added to market worries. Factory production slowed in October, while consumer spending remained weak. This has raised questions about how long exports can continue to support growth in the world's second-largest economy."China's policy measures to combat deflation continue to be incremental and we remain below consensus for China EPS growth," Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note cited by Reuters.They added that stock valuations offered only limited support, making it better to pick individual stocks rather than invest across the wider market.However, some sectors managed to stay in positive territory. The CSI300 Financial Index gained 1.5%, while consumer staples shares rose 1.2%, against the broader decline in Chinese markets.Concerns over the AI industry also dragged down other Asian markets on Monday. Investors were watching for signals about the future of the global AI industry ahead of Nvidia's earnings report, due on Tuesday, and Anthropic's major stock market debut later this week. US equity futures were also trading lower.South Korea's Kospi fell 2.8% to 5,142.84, dragged down by losses in major memory chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. SK Hynix shares dropped 5.5%, while Samsung Electronics fell 3.2%.Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 1.6% to 60,182.50 after official data released on Monday showed that the country's economy had contracted in the latest quarter. Among major technology stocks, SoftBank Group, an investor in OpenAI, slipped 4.2%. Memory maker Kioxia Holdings lost 5.5%, while chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron fell 5.2%.Taiwan's Taiex dropped 4.1%, while shares of its leading chipmaker, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), declined 3.4%.Concerns about whether companies will continue spending heavily on AI had been growing even before the developments at Nvidia, analysts said. Uncertainty over the development of AI data centres in the US had also increased following the US midterm elections. Investors are now watching Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO for further signals about the strength of the AI industry.
Article Summary: China's stock markets ended lower on Monday, with technology shares leading the decline. Weak domestic economic data added to investor concerns, leaving key indices hovering near their lowest levels since July 2025. The fall came as worries over the future of the global AI boom continued to weigh on markets.

Article Title: Indian refiners set to benefit as global diesel inventories hit fresh lows: Report
Article Text:
Representative image

Tight diesel market supports refining margins

ONGC , Oil India face production and policy concerns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

European gas inventories remain below seasonal averages

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you feel about the performance of ONGC and Oil India compared to global energy companies? They are performing poorly They are performing adequately They are performing well 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Indian oil refiners could benefit from tightening global diesel supplies and sustained refining margins even if crude oil prices moderate, as falling exports from China and declining inventories in major markets are expected to support profitability, according to a report by Equirus Research.In its latest Oil & Gas Weekly Tracker, the brokerage said the tightening global diesel market could strengthen refining margins, particularly benefiting standalone refiners such as Reliance Industries The report highlighted a sharp decline in China's diesel exports, which are expected to fall below 0.8 million tonnes in November 2026. This compares with 1.33 million tonnes in August and 1.8 million tonnes in September.China's commercial diesel inventories have also fallen to 11.1 million tonnes at the end of October, their lowest level since records began in 2011.Lower exports from China, combined with declining diesel inventories in the United States and other major markets, could intensify competition for available supplies and support global refining margins, Equirus said.Strong diesel cracks have already contributed to refining profitability, the brokerage noted. Diesel cracks refer to the difference between crude oil prices and the prices of refined diesel and are an important indicator of how much refiners earn from processing crude.Equirus expects sustained tightness in the global diesel market to remain favourable for Indian refiners, even if crude prices ease.The outlook comes as India's upstream oil producers continue to face challenges despite movements in international crude prices.According to the report, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) and Oil India have underperformed global energy companies, with their stock performance reflecting concerns over government interventions, production growth and their ability to retain the benefits of higher crude prices.Equirus pointed to previous government interventions, including crude discounts provided by upstream companies to oil marketing companies during earlier periods of high crude prices. The introduction of windfall taxes in 2022 was another factor cited by the brokerage.These developments have created continuing uncertainty for domestic upstream producers, with concerns that additional profits could be shared with the government weighing on investor sentiment, the report said.Muted production growth, particularly at ONGC, is another challenge. Natural declines in output from existing fields and delays in bringing new projects on stream have restricted the ability of upstream companies to increase production.The brokerage also flagged tightness in global gas markets as an important factor to watch in the coming quarters.Europe's gas storage facilities were around 71 per cent full, with net withdrawals already under way. Inventories were also materially below seasonal averages, according to the report.The assessment highlights the contrasting outlook across India's oil and gas sector, with tighter diesel supplies supporting refining margins while domestic upstream producers continue to contend with production and policy-related concerns.
Article Summary: Indian oil refiners could benefit from tightening global diesel supplies and sustained refining margins. Falling exports from China and declining inventories in major markets are expected to support profitability. ONGC and Oil India have underperformed global energy companies. Domestic upstream producers continue to contend with production and policy-related concerns. European gas inventories remain below seasonal averages.

Article Title: India has up to 607 tonnes of primary gold metal but imported over 800 tonnes of gold in FY26 worth a record $71.98 billion; now world’s fifth largest gold importer to focus on ramping up gold mining
Article Text:
Now, Niti Aayog is considering a blueprint to boost gold exploration and mining in India. (Image for representative purpose only)

India’s gold mining focus

India’s gold reserves for mining

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is estimated to have around 501 million to 518 million tonnes of primary gold ore resources, containing an estimated 600 to 607 tonnes of primary gold metal. Yet, it continues to import gold in a big way. In fact, India is the world’s fifth largest gold importer.Despite the country’s gold resources, mining activity has yet to gain significant momentum. Gaps in geological information, inadequate exploration, lengthy project development periods, the design of mining auctions and the lack of commercial viability of projects have discouraged investors from entering the sector.Now, Niti Aayog is considering a blueprint to boost gold exploration and mining in India, with the aim of attracting investment into the sector as the country continues to import large quantities of the precious metal every year, people familiar with the discussions told ET.The proposed framework is expected to suggest fiscal incentives for gold mining and changes to the regulatory regime. These could include longer-term mining rights and a system for rating bidders, intended to draw investment while ensuring that companies have the technical capabilities needed to develop India’s gold resources sustainably, the people said.The blueprint is also likely to focus on simplifying regulatory clearances through better coordination between the Centre and state governments.Other proposed measures include adopting internationally accepted reporting standards to strengthen the quality of geological data and establishing a stable, predictable policy regime to make projects more attractive to lenders and investors.Last week, Niti Aayog vice chairman Ashok Kumar Lahiri discussed a draft report titled ‘India’s Gold Mining Policy: Challenges, Learning and the Road Ahead’. Prepared by Pahle India Foundation (PIF) with support from the World Gold Council (WGC), the report examines the challenges facing the sector and the steps needed to address them. The discussions focused on how its key recommendations could be incorporated into India’s gold mining policy.Although the official think tank has reached agreement on the broader macroeconomic recommendations, it has sought more detailed inputs from PIF on specific aspects of the proposed framework.These include identifying credible bidders, ensuring that mining projects are financially viable and improving access to geospatial data to make the sector more attractive to investors, one of the people cited above said.Bihar accounts for the largest share of India’s known gold reserves at 44-45%, followed by Rajasthan at 25% and Karnataka at 21%. West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh account for 3% each, while Jharkhand holds 2%.India’s gold imports fell 39.9% year-on-year to $24.78 billion during April-October 2026, compared with $41.24 billion in the corresponding period, as global gold prices corrected to below $4,000 per ounce.Despite the decline, India remains the world’s fifth-largest gold importer, accounting for around 6.7% to more than 9% of the value of global gold imports.The country’s gold imports touched an all-time high of $71.98 billion, equivalent to more than 800 tonnes, in 2025-26. Switzerland was the largest source of these imports, contributing 34-40% of the total.
Article Summary: India is estimated to have around 501 million to 518 million tonnes of primary gold ore resources. Yet, it continues to import gold in a big way. Now, Niti Aayog is considering a blueprint to boost gold exploration and mining in India.

Article Title: Wholesale inflation jumps to 12.29% in October due to rising crude and power prices
Article Text:
Wholesale inflation jumps to 12.29%

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Wholesale inflation gathered pace in October, with the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) rising 12.29% year-on-year, compared with 11.39% in September. The increase was largely driven by a steep rise in fuel and power prices, which recorded a much sharper inflation rate during the month, according to data released by the ministry of commerce and industry on Monday.The fuel and power category saw inflation jump to 32.84% in October from 25.85% in September. Primary articles also reported a higher inflation rate, while manufactured products offered some relief with a marginal moderation.The increase in fuel and power inflation was led by a sharp acceleration in crude petroleum and natural gas prices. Inflation in this category rose to 70.80% in October, significantly higher than the 57.32% recorded in September.Mineral oils also remained a major contributor, with inflation increasing to 45.57% from 40.02% in the previous month. Electricity prices saw a turnaround, recording inflation of 8.06% in October after registering a contraction of 0.43% in September.The ministry identified mineral oils, crude petroleum and natural gas, and electricity among the key drivers of wholesale inflation during the month.Inflation in primary food articles edged up to 8.26% in October from 8.14% in September.However, the broader WPI Food Index showed a marginal easing.The index, which includes both food articles and manufactured food products, recorded inflation of 8.58% in October, compared with 8.66% in the previous month.Food articles and food products were among the key contributors to wholesale price inflation, according to the ministry.The manufactured products category recorded a marginal moderation in inflation, easing to 9.54% in October from 9.76% in September. However, some key segments within the category continued to see price pressures.Inflation in basic metals increased to 17.21% from 16.96% in September. Chemicals and chemical products also saw a rise, with inflation climbing to 17.53% from 16.74%.In contrast, manufactured food products recorded a moderation in inflation, which eased to 9.24% in October from 9.44% in the previous month.The cumulative WPI inflation rate for the April-October period of the current financial year stood at 10.14%. This is in contrast to a contraction of 0.30% recorded during the corresponding period of the previous financial year.During the seven-month period, fuel and power inflation stood at 26.37%, while manufactured products recorded inflation of 8.37%. The ministry said the October WPI figures are provisional and were compiled with a weighted response rate of 81.1%.
Article Summary: The Wholesale Price Index (WPI) rose 12.29% year-on-year, compared with 11.39% in September. The increase was largely driven by a steep rise in fuel and power prices. Primary articles also reported a higher inflation rate, while manufactured products offered some relief.

Article Title: Jimmy Tata, Ratan Tata’s younger brother, backs N Chandrasekaran’s reappointment & Tata Sons listing
Article Text:
His backing for Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and the RBI’s listing requirement places him on the opposite side of the debate from Noel Tata. (File photo of N Chandrasekaran)

Who is Jimmy Tata?

Favours Chandrasekaran’s reappointment

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a fresh development in the Tata group tussle, Jimmy Naval Tata has supported the continuation of N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman for a third term. Jimmy Tata is the younger brother of the late Tata group patriarch Ratan Tata. He is also the longest-serving perpetual trustee of Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT).His views have come to light as the Tata group faces an intensifying battle over control. The Tata Sons board and Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, the company’s majority shareholder, have been at loggerheads over several issues.Not only that, Jimmy Tata has also backed the Reserve Bank of India ’s position that the group’s holding company should meet the listing requirements prescribed for upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs), people familiar with the matter told ET.Jimmy is the younger son of Naval Tata and his first wife, Sooni Commissariat. Noel Tata, born to Naval Tata and his second wife, Simone Dunoyer, is Jimmy’s half-brother.He is the second-largest individual shareholder of Tata Sons after Noel Tata, with a 0.81% stake in the company, equivalent to 3,262 shares. An analysis by the financial daily, based on estimates provided by investment bankers, has valued his holding at between Rs 7,000 crore and Rs 10,000 crore.Jimmy Tata has been associated with SRTT as a trustee since 1989 and is one of its three perpetual trustees, alongside Noel Tata and Jehangir Jehangir.He also serves as a trustee of the Bai Hirabai Jamsetji Tata Navsari Charitable Institution and Sarvajanik Seva Trust. Both are among the charitable trusts operating under the Tata Trusts umbrella.The 85-year-old, who leads a reclusive life in Pune and has seldom participated in or voted at Tata Trusts meetings, is understood to have shared these views in a documented exchange with another trustee.That trustee subsequently briefed a few others on the conversation, the people quoted in the report said. Jimmy Tata has also expressed his views on the functioning and governance of Tata Trusts.Jimmy Tata and fellow Pune resident Jehangir Jehangir have remained among the least visible members of the Tata trustee community. Neither has publicly disclosed their position on the ongoing struggle over control of the Tata group.Although Jimmy Tata generally avoids attending trustee meetings and voting on matters, he has been known to communicate extensively with trustees and board members through correspondence, setting out his positions on a range of subjects in considerable detail. In a 2016 interview, he gave reporters from The Times of India a file containing hundreds of such letters.It is not known whether Jimmy Tata has continued writing to trustees and board members in recent years, particularly after leaving his Colaba apartment and retreating into a more private life in Pune. His last public appearance was during the funeral and associated events following the death of Ratan Tata in late 2024. Under Ratan Tata’s will, a share in the family’s Juhu Bungalow was bequeathed to Jimmy.According to people familiar with the matter, Jimmy Tata has continued to keep a close watch on developments within the trusts, including the disagreements and disputes that have surfaced since his elder brother’s death.During his recent exchange with a fellow trustee, Jimmy Tata reportedly voiced concern over what he considers a deterioration in the standards of the institutions. He is understood to have called for them to return to the principles and objectives that guided their establishment, the people said.It remains uncertain whether his views will have any immediate impact on the current developments. Their influence could depend on whether he decides to exercise his voting rights at SRTT meetings.Jimmy Tata is also understood to favour limiting representation of the Tata family on the boards of the trusts to a single member, instead of allowing several family members to hold positions of influence. He is understood to have stressed that the institutions were created to serve the country and support nation-building, and that their operations should be guided by these philanthropic and public-interest goals rather than family interests.His backing for Chandrasekaran’s reappointment and the RBI’s listing requirement places him on the opposite side of the debate from Noel Tata. Noel has opposed both the proposed listing of Tata Sons and Chandrasekaran’s continuation as chairman. The differences highlight a wider disagreement over leadership, governance and the ownership structure of the group’s holding company.Together, the Tata Trusts hold around 66% of Tata Sons, of which SRTT owns 23.56%. This gives the trusts a pivotal role in decisions affecting the future of Tata Sons and the broader conglomerate.The RBI has maintained that Tata Sons, which is classified as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC), must adhere to the applicable regulatory requirements, including listing its shares on a recognised stock exchange.Under RBI regulations, an NBFC designated as an upper-layer entity must list its equity shares within three years of being placed in that category. Tata Sons falls under this classification, and the central bank has rejected its application to surrender its registration as a core investment company.
Article Summary: Jimmy Naval Tata has supported the continuation of N Chandrasekaran as Tata Sons chairman for a third term. He has also backed the Reserve Bank of India ’s position that the group’s holding company should meet the listing requirements prescribed for upper-layer non-banking financial companies (NBFCs)

Article Title: Did Nvidia row push for a united anti-China stance? US, India sign accord to protect AI suppy chain: Report
Article Text:
India has joined a US-led agreement to protect critical technologies and AI supply chains through greater cooperation among partner nations as Washington seeks to counter China's growing influence in strategic sectors.

What is Pax Silica?

India-US cooperation on critical technologies

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India has joined the United States and several other countries in signing the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity, an agreement aimed at protecting critical technologies and artificial intelligence supply chains amid growing competition with China.US under-secretary of state for economic affairs Jacob Helberg said India, South Korea, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates had signed the declaration, according to a Financial Times report. Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission were expected to sign it the following week.Explaining the need for cooperation, Helberg told the Financial Times that AI supply chains span several countries, making their security a shared concern. “The know how to design a chip, the machine that makes it and the port that ships it can all be in different countries,” he said.“What makes the San Francisco Declaration historic is that Pax Silica partners have agreed to treat the security of those technologies and the infrastructure behind them as a shared responsibility,” Helberg added.The declaration, signed by the US and partners including Japan, Australia, Israel and the United Kingdom, seeks to establish a joint list of critical technologies and supply chains that underpin AI and require greater protection.These include semiconductors, critical minerals, energy infrastructure and advanced manufacturing.The declaration is part of Pax Silica, a US-led initiative launched in December 2025 by Helberg. It is the US state department's flagship effort to strengthen cooperation among partner countries on AI-related supply chains, including critical minerals, energy inputs, semiconductor manufacturing and AI infrastructure.The initiative has expanded its membership through the 2026 summit, with Argentina, Chile, Costa Rica, El Salvador, the European Union, Germany, Greece, Kazakhstan, the Netherlands and Panama among the latest additions to the Pax Silica Declaration. The number of signatories has risen to 24, including India, Australia, Finland, Israel, Japan, Norway, Qatar, South Korea, Singapore, Sweden, the Philippines, the UAE and the UK.The latest development comes amid expanding cooperation between India and the US on critical technologies and trusted infrastructure.Earlier this month, foreign ministers of the Quad grouping - India, the US, Japan and Australia - announced plans to provide more than $85 million in technical and financial assistance to expand access to trusted AI infrastructure across the Indo-Pacific.The announcement followed a meeting of the four countries' foreign ministers on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers' Summit in Georgia. US secretary of state Marco Rubio, external affairs minister S Jaishankar, Japanese foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Australian foreign minister Penny Wong attended the meeting.Washington also announced a separate $10 million allocation to support critical minerals recycling initiatives in India and ASEAN member states.The declaration comes ahead of a planned meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen this week.The development comes at a time when concerns are mounting over the sustainability of the AI spending boom, particularly the massive investments being made by technology companies in Nvidia's chips and data centre infrastructure. Questions over whether these investments will generate adequate returns have weighed on investor sentiment, while the reported leadership uncertainty after Jensen Huang's exit at Nvidia has added to concerns about the outlook for the AI sector. As one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom, Nvidia's performance and leadership remain closely watched for signals on the pace of future AI spending.
Article Summary: India has joined the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity. The agreement is aimed at protecting critical technologies and artificial intelligence supply chains amid growing competition with China. The declaration is part of Pax Silica, a US-led initiative launched in December 2025.

Article Title: AI agents could help banks generate nearly 3x returns over three years: McKinsey
Article Text:
Representative image

AI productivity gains have yet to translate into significant earnings

Rising costs and security risks pose challenges

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Banks adopting artificial intelligence (AI) agents could recover their investments in around 10 months and generate returns of nearly three times the initial outlay over three years, according to a report by McKinsey, which highlighted the technology's potential to reshape the banking sector.An analysis of 52 agentic AI use cases in banking found that the average investment payback period was approximately 10 months, while the estimated return on investment over three years stood at around 2.9 times, the report said.McKinsey said banks' competitive advantage would increasingly depend on how quickly they move beyond pilot projects and integrate AI into their operations, products and customer services.“The economics of banking may shift in quarters rather than years as AI changes what the work costs, how a bank and its customers interact, and how those customers choose,” the report said.Despite the potential returns, McKinsey cautioned that improvements in employee productivity do not automatically lead to higher profits for banks.According to its 2026 State of AI survey, 80 per cent of respondents reported individual productivity gains from using AI.However, only 6 per cent said the technology accounted for a significant share of their earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT).The findings suggest a gap between the productivity benefits reported by employees and the financial gains being realised by organisations.Customer adoption of AI is also increasing. A survey of around 46,000 consumers across 13 countries found that 23 per cent were already using generative AI for banking-related tasks.Among those using AI for such activities, 74 per cent relied on platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, indicating the role of external AI tools in customers' banking-related interactions.The report also flagged the financial and security risks associated with wider AI adoption. Spending on AI tokens, computing and operations could rise to as much as 20 per cent of labour costs, adding to the expenses banks would need to manage while deploying the technology.It also cited around USD 900 million in reported losses from AI-enabled crime recorded by the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) in 2025.McKinsey said banks would need to build what it described as institutional intelligence by bringing together reliable data, customer information, internal policies and the experience of senior employees.Data readiness remains a significant hurdle. As many as 48 per cent of banking executives surveyed identified it as their biggest obstacle to adopting AI.The report said banks would also need to establish clear permissions, continuous monitoring and human oversight to ensure AI agents operate safely.It added that institutions would be better positioned to capture the benefits of the technology if they redesigned entire business processes rather than simply automating individual tasks.
Article Summary: Banks adopting artificial intelligence (AI) agents could recover their investments in around 10 months and generate returns of nearly three times the initial outlay over three years, according to a report by McKinsey. Despite the potential returns, McKinsey cautioned that improvements in employee productivity do not automatically lead to higher profits.

Article Title: New Zealand launches six-month graduate work visa today: Who among Indian students can apply?
Article Text:
New Zealand opens six-month Graduate Work Visa applications for international students, including Indians. (AI Image)

Three-month application deadline

What can graduates do under the new visa?

How to apply and what is the fee?

Can graduates extend their stay?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Zealand has opened applications for its new six-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa from November 16, 2026, giving eligible international graduates, including Indian students, an opportunity to stay and work in the country after completing their studies.Announced by Immigration New Zealand in September, the new visa is aimed at students who have completed eligible qualifications in New Zealand but do not meet the requirements for a Post-Study Work Visa. It allows graduates to work for any employer for up to six months while searching for employment and exploring longer-term work opportunities.Indian students who have completed a qualification at Level 5, 6 or 7 of the New Zealand Qualifications and Credentials Framework (NZQCF) can apply, subject to the immigration authority's eligibility requirements.To qualify, applicants must have studied full-time in New Zealand for a minimum of 24 weeks. Their qualification must not be in English language studies, foundation or bridging programmes. Micro-credentials are also excluded. Students whose qualifications make them eligible for a Post-Study Work Visa cannot apply under the new category.One of the key conditions is the application deadline. Graduates must apply within three months of the expiry of their student visa for the qualification on which their application is based.They must also have held a student visa for that qualification within the three months before applying.Applicants will need to demonstrate that they have at least NZD $5,000 in available funds to support themselves during their stay. They must meet New Zealand's health and character requirements and may be asked to submit medical certificates, chest X-rays or police certificates, depending on their circumstances.Students whose studies were funded under the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarship Programme must also obtain written approval from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade or Education New Zealand.The Short-Term Graduate Work Visa provides open work rights for six months. Holders can take up employment with any employer in New Zealand, provided the work is covered by an employment agreement or a contract for services.However, the visa does not permit holders to establish or operate a business as owners. It also does not allow them to provide commercial sexual services.The visa cannot be used to include a spouse or dependent children in the application. Holders can support visitor visa applications for their partners and dependent children. However, family members cannot obtain work or student visas solely on the basis of their relationship with the visa holder. Partners may apply for work visas independently, while dependent children can apply for student visas as international students.Applications can be submitted online through Immigration New Zealand's Enhanced Immigration Online system (ADEPT), which opened for applications on November 16.Students must upload their qualification certificate, academic transcript or a letter from their education provider confirming completion of the programme or eligibility to graduate. They must also provide passport details, an acceptable photograph and evidence of sufficient funds.The visa fee starts at NZD $1,670. The final cost depends on the applicant's country and place of application.Immigration New Zealand has specified that applicants can be granted only one Short-Term Graduate Work Visa. The six-month visa cannot be extended, and holders cannot apply for another visa under the same category.Those seeking to remain in New Zealand beyond the permitted period will need to obtain another visa before their current visa expires.Former Short-Term Graduate Work Visa holders can apply for another student visa only if their proposed programme is a bachelor's degree or a qualification at a higher NZQCF level than the one used for their graduate work visa, and the new qualification makes them eligible for a Post-Study Work Visa.Further information on eligibility, application requirements and visa conditions is available on Immigration New Zealand's official website: https://www.immigration.govt.nz/visas/short-term-graduate-work-visa/.
Article Summary: New Zealand has opened applications for its new six-month Short-Term Graduate Work Visa from November 16, 2026. The new visa is aimed at students who have completed eligible qualifications in New Zealand but do not meet the requirements for a Post-Study Work Visa. It allows graduates to work for any employer for up to six months while searching for employment.

Article Title: 'It's acceptable to throw oneself into work...': Barack Obama challenges the idea of work-life balance; says success comes with trade-offs
Article Text:
Barack Obama with his family. (Instagram/@Barack Obama)

The Pivot Podcast

The price of a campaign

The 6:30 PM rule

A ledger, not a balance

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Pivot Podcast

The modern workplace sells a tidy promise called balance. Barack Obama , who held one of the most demanding jobs in the world for two terms, says the promise is incomplete at best.Speaking onin 2024, the former president said excellence in any field, whether sports, music, business or politics, comes with seasons when a person is “out of balance” and “single-minded”. Anyone chasing a serious career goal, by his account, should expect long hours and working lunches.Obama learned this the hard way. When he first ran for president, he worked relentlessly for over a year and a half. Weekends offered some respite. Michelle Obama , who had a full-time job of her own, absorbed much of the domestic load, including the care of their daughters, Sasha and Malia.The effort led to two terms in the White House. It was also not sustainable, and Obama has said so himself.As president, he set a rule: dinner with his family every night at 6:30 PM, even if he returned to work afterwards. Some leaders might see that as lost time. Obama argued the opposite.“They ground you and give you perspective, and over time, that makes you better,” he said.At an Obama Foundation event in 2019, the former president was sharp about priorities. “I don’t think there’s a perfect formula,” he said, adding that on his deathbed he would not remember “any bill I passed” or “any speech I gave”.That is not a dismissal of ambition. He said the level of commitment a person can give to work depends on what life at home looks like, and the reverse holds too.“There will be phases in your life where you have to prioritize different things,” Obama said. There are times, he said, when it is acceptable to throw oneself into work because everything at home is in a good place. There are other times when work must give way because things at home are not.The same logic applies to couples. When one partner chases a dream, the other covers the gap, and the favour must be returned. “You can have it all, but you can’t have it all at once,” he told, referring to himself and Michelle. The aim, he said, is to “create some equity inside the family”.Balance, in Obama’s telling, is not a daily state to be achieved. It is a ledger kept over years. Debts are permitted, provided they are repaid.
Article Summary: Barack Obama says excellence in any field comes with seasons when a person is ‘out of balance’ and ‘single-minded’ Anyone chasing a serious career goal, by his account, should expect long hours and working lunches.

Article Title: Sen-sational turnaround: Lakshya fights back from one game down to lift Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Lakshya Sen came from a game down to beat Japan's Koki Watanabe in the men's singles final and win the Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title in Kumamoto on Sunday.The world No. 13 lost the opening game but fought back to win the next two and seal a 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 victory in one hour and four minutes.Sen took control in the deciding game after opening up a 11-7 lead. He extended his advantage to nine points and did not allow Watanabe to fight his way back into the contest.The title comes shortly after Sen won the Hylo Open in Germany. His victory in Kumamoto also earned him 9,200 ranking points.Watanabe opened up a 3-0 lead, with Lakshya being a tad laid-back initially. The Japanese nailed his smashes to perfection, varying the pace. He repeatedly produced straight down-the-line smashes on Lakshya's forehand side to move to 6-1. Lakshya cut down the lead to 5-8.A judgement error and then a wide return made it 5-10. An angled smash from the Indian was followed by a net error as Watanabe took a five-point advantage into the break.On resumption, Lakshya fought his way back to 10-12, with the Indian producing a straight smash and a defensive block. Another superb return-to-serve helped him close the gap to 11-12.The Indian dived to save a point, only to send the shuttle long. Another shot going long took Watanabe to a 15-11 lead.Watanabe looked in control as he continued to find winners to establish a six-point lead at 18-12. The Japanese soon grabbed eight game points with another straight return. The Indian saved one before going wide.A change of sides brought a change of fortune as Lakshya surged to a 5-0 lead. The Indian took control of the net and didn't allow his opponent to find his way. He pounced on a loose net shot, and a net error from his opponent helped him maintain his 5-0 lead. A perfect cross-court smash earned him a five-point lead at the break.Despite a few errors, Lakshya's quick racquet speed helped him maintain his lead at 15-10. Watanabe also committed many errors, hitting wide and into the net, to leave the Indian three points away from forcing a decider.The Japanese fought back from 10-19 to make it 17-19, but Lakshya soon grabbed three game points with a fast push. He sent one shot long before unleashing another thunderous and precise smash to roar back into the contest.In the decider, a full-stretch dive to produce a defensive block gave Lakshya a 2-1 lead as the two played some fascinating rallies.The rallies got tighter and the score closer as the two battled hard to take control. From 3-3, Lakshya opened up a 9-6 lead before producing another pinpoint smash.The Indian took a four-point cushion at the interval after a push that seemed to be going wide managed to find its spot.Two brutal smashes extended Lakshya's lead to 13-7. Attack was the word as Lakshya kept producing attacking returns to leave his opponent dazed.Another steep winner to his opponent's backhand, followed by another lethal smash, took him to 16-7, leaving the local fans silent.From 7-17, Watanabe again fought back to 13-19 before Lakshya found two perfect returns to earn seven match points. He sealed the match on the second occasion with another cross-court winner.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen beats Koki Watanabe to win the Kumamoto Masters Japan Open title. The world No. 13 lost the opening game but fought back to win next two. Sen took control in the deciding game after opening up a 11-7 lead.

Article Title: Anthropic is eyeing a mega IPO, but will investors buy its trillion-dollar AI dream?
Article Text:
Anthropic's trillion-dollar IPO dream

Tech IPO scorecard: Big gains, bigger setbacks

Revenue is soaring, but so are the costs

More shares could enter the market from day one

AI investment faces the returns question

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Will Anthropic's IPO be a market blockbuster or another case of early fireworks fading fast?The Claude parent’s proposed $1.4 trillion listing comes at a time when recent technology IPOs have delivered sharply contrasting returns, leaving investors with little indication of what could lie ahead.An analysis by S&P Global Market Intelligence of seven major recent US technology IPOs found that four were trading above their offer prices a year after listing, while the other three had suffered significant losses. The contrasting returns offer little certainty about how Anthropic's shares will perform if its proposed Nasdaq listing goes ahead.The AI company plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece, according to an amended registration statement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 10. At the upper end of the price band, the offering could fetch $64.35 billion, placing Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at around $1.4 trillion. Its shares are expected to trade under the ticker ANT.This would put the company above its $965 billion valuation from a May funding round, although below the approximately $2 trillion it was reportedly aiming for earlier this year.The first-year performance of recent listings has been far from uniform.Arm Holdings topped the S&P analysis, delivering a 171.4 per cent return after its September 2023 listing. Snowflake and Airbnb were not far behind, gaining 169.6 per cent and 165.3 per cent, respectively. DoorDash also posted a positive return of 61.6 per cent.The picture was less encouraging for Lyft, Uber and Rivian. Their shares fell 62.6 per cent, 29.7 per cent and 57.7 per cent, respectively, amid market disruptions and rising interest rates.Even some of the biggest recent offerings have struggled to maintain their initial momentum. SpaceX, which raised $135 per share in June in the largest IPO on record, witnessed a surge in its stock during the first two trading sessions. However, the rally subsequently lost steam.On June 18, its shares dropped 6.5 per cent as investors booked profits and weighed the company's high valuation against the costs of expanding its AI operations. By November 11, the stock was 13.2 per cent below its offer price, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence.South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix also saw early gains give way to a correction after its Nasdaq debut in July. Its American depositary receipts (ADRs), which were priced at $149, rose 12.8 per cent on the first trading day before falling nearly 8 per cent on the second as investors booked profits.Anthropic's financial numbers present another important consideration ahead of its proposed market debut. The company reported revenue of $33.24 billion in the first nine months of 2026, significantly higher than the $4.58 billion recorded for the whole of 2025.Its third-quarter revenue stood at around $17 billion, registering a 47 per cent increase over the previous quarter. However, the revenue growth comes alongside substantial losses and infrastructure spending.Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026. Its infrastructure commitments stood at around $895 billion, including $69.8 billion payable within 12 months.The number of shares available for trading could also become a point of focus after the listing. Anthropic's employees and early investors will be allowed to sell some of their holdings from the first day of trading, instead of being bound by the standard 180-day lock-up period.There is also another component to the IPO's funding arrangements. Seven of the company's computing suppliers have agreed to buy a combined $26 billion worth of non-voting Class N shares at the IPO price.Anthropic's proposed debut comes as investors take a closer look at whether massive investments in artificial intelligence are translating into revenue at the pace expected.Recent third-quarter earnings have brought capital expenditure and the ability of companies to generate returns from AI spending into sharper focus. Regulatory uncertainty following the US midterm elections has added another concern for the sector.With recent technology listings showing that first-day excitement does not always guarantee sustained stock market gains, Anthropic's proposed IPO will bring its valuation, financial losses and infrastructure commitments under investor scrutiny.
Article Summary: Anthropic plans to put 825 million Class A shares on the market at $70-78 apiece. At the upper end of the price band, the offering could fetch $64.35 billion. This would put Anthropic's fully diluted valuation at around $1.4 trillion.

Article Title: Debt, dues and deja vu: How poor nations end up paying more than they borrow
Article Text:
Developing countries' external debt hits record $9.4 trillion

Countries pay more than they receive

Poorest countries face highest borrowing costs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Private lending and bond sales pick up

The debt burden on low and middle-income countries continues to rise, with repayments becoming more expensive and fresh loans costing more. Their external debt reached a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, as countries paid more towards existing loans than they received in new funding. Borrowing costs also hit their highest levels in decades for some of the poorest economies, according to a World Bank report.The World Bank's International Debt Report 2026 said external debt increased 5.5 per cent from $8.9 trillion in 2024. This was the biggest annual rise since 2021. The increase was driven by higher borrowing, a recovery in lending from private lenders and a weaker US dollar, which raised the reported value of debt.The growing debt has increased the amount countries need to spend on repayments. In 2025, low- and middle-income countries spent $1.4 trillion on servicing their debt, which includes both principal and interest payments. This was 1.9 per cent more than in 2024 and the fifth consecutive annual increase.The amount paid towards debt was also much higher than the fresh funding received. Between 2022 and 2025, these countries paid around $436.1 billion more in debt repayments than they received in new financing.Payments to bondholders alone rose 13.7 per cent to $363.1 billion in 2025.Highlighting the pressure on poorer nations, the World Bank said, “The countries that can least afford it are paying the most to borrow.”Countries eligible for funding from the International Development Association (IDA) faced particularly high borrowing costs. They paid an average interest rate of 8.2 per cent on new loans in 2025, the highest level since the late 1980s.Borrowing money from bondholders was even more expensive, with interest rates averaging 9.4 per cent during the year.However, the trend was different for countries borrowing from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Their average interest rate fell to 5.5 per cent in 2025, compared with 5.8 per cent in 2024.Lending by private creditors to developing economies also increased in 2025. The debt owed by low- and middle-income countries to private lenders rose 5.2 per cent to $5 trillion.Governments also raised more money through bond sales. Public-sector bond issuances jumped 34.6 per cent to $250.6 billion, the highest level since 2021, the report said.This activity has continued in 2026.Preliminary figures for January to August show that countries continued to issue bonds despite high borrowing costs. Several countries had already issued more bonds in the first eight months of 2026 than they had during the whole of 2025.The World Bank warned that rising debt repayments and high funding needs are leaving governments with less money to manage their finances. This is also increasing the risks linked to rising debt and the need to refinance existing loans.
Article Summary: Developing countries' external debt hits record $9.4 trillion in 2025. Countries paid more towards existing loans than they received in new funding. Borrowing costs also hit their highest levels in decades for some of the poorest economies. World Bank warned that rising debt repayments and high funding needs are leaving governments with less money to manage their finances.

Article Title: Intel sued by shareholders after stock plunges 29% in a single day, wipes out $140 billion
Article Text:
The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations

Why shareholders have sued Intel

Intel shares remain under pressure

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Intel has been hit with a shareholder lawsuit accusing the US chipmaker of concealing mounting problems in its personal computer business, weeks before a disappointing financial forecast triggered a massive stock sell-off that wiped out nearly $140 billion in market value in a single day.The proposed class-action lawsuit, filed in a federal court in San Jose, California, on Friday, alleges that Intel misled investors by failing to disclose the extent to which slowing PC sales and an inventory glut were weighing on its business. The company's shares plunged 28.6% on October 30, marking their steepest single-day decline in decades and one of the biggest blows to its market valuation.The lawsuit has been brought by shareholders led by the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System, a Michigan pension fund. Intel chief executive Lip-Bu Tan and chief financial officer David Zinsner have also been named as defendants. The plaintiffs are seeking unspecified damages on behalf of investors who purchased Intel shares between July 23 and October 29.According to the complaint, Intel was too slow to inform investors about the impact of weakening PC demand and excess inventory on its revenue prospects. Shareholders argued that these problems outweighed the potential gains from the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, including increased investment in data centres.The lawsuit also alleges that Intel had both the motive and opportunity to defraud investors when it raised capital in mid-August, halfway through what the plaintiffs described as a 'disastrous' third quarter. The company sold $23 billion worth of stock at $95 per share as it sought to expand its chip contract manufacturing business, a key component of Tan's strategy.The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations. The following day, its shares crashed 28.6%, erasing approximately $140 billion in market value.During an earnings call, Tan expressed disappointment over manufacturing supply shortages, an 'unprecedented memory crunch' and the resulting weakness in PC demand.'We need to address these challenges with urgency,' he told analysts.Intel has invested heavily in expanding its manufacturing capabilities, hoping to capitalise on growing demand for chips used in AI data centres. However, supply disruptions have made it difficult for the company to benefit fully from that demand. At the same time, rising memory prices have pushed up PC costs, further weighing on consumer demand.The October sell-off has continued to cast a shadow over Intel's stock, even as the broader market has shown signs of resilience. The company's shares came under renewed pressure during the following trading sessions, falling further amid a wider rout in semiconductor stocks.According to Yahoo Finance calculations, chip and memory companies collectively lost more than $400 billion in market value in a single session during the recent downturn. Intel was among the biggest casualties, with its market value falling sharply from its September levels.Intel shares closed at $59.66 on Friday, November 13. Despite the recent losses, the stock remains up 62% so far this year, although it has retreated significantly from its June 30 peak of $142.35.
Article Summary: The proposed class-action lawsuit alleges that Intel misled investors by failing to disclose the extent to which slowing PC sales and an inventory glut were weighing on its business. The allegations come after Intel's October 29 earnings outlook fell short of Wall Street expectations. The following day, its shares crashed 28.6%, erasing approximately $140 billion in market value.

Article Title: Jensen Huang plots return as Nvidia CEO; Musk, 158,000 others sign petition backing comeback
Article Text:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is reportedly pushing for a return to the company (File photo/Reuters)

Also Read |

Also Read |
